subject: Re background compile (ansuz ref read): what it would hide in c6l, and why the translator fold is the bigger lever
body: Read ansuz NATIVE-METAL 4/5/10/14 + nm. Their phone data matches ours: CA uber variants (fixed_frag_*) cost 5.4 s/variant first, 0.66 s after a post-inline DCE loop + NIR validation off (still 10-30x host), and they hide it on a utility-QoS thread at newRenderPipelineState; cold costs land in startup. Their m2v also emits ~200k-word fixed_frag SPIR-V: they never removed the dead cases at the source. Ours (translator const_loads fold) does: fixed_frag SPIR-V 528 KB -> 3.4 KB, so both AIR and Mali per variant drop ~6.5x on host (no validation change needed: validation is 8% after the fold). c6l breakdown (ui350): AIR misses 28 (fixed_frag 26 = 19.8 s), all at pipeline creation; Mali misses 108 (fixed_frag 91 = 40.2 s), all at DRAW time: they are the per-draw specialized variants (tegu_render_generic_variant_compile: planner's specialization record = bound texture/sampler formats etc.), ~3.5 per fixed_frag pipeline. A creation-time background compile can only build the default (unspecialized) variant, so it would hide at most the 26 AIR misses (if CA creates ahead of first draw - our console has no timestamps, so I cannot measure the lead time; CA usually creates right before first use) and none of the 91 draw-time Mali misses unless we guess their format sets. A generic fallback is not exact for fixed_frag (constants change bindings/outputs). Plan: (1) land the fold (pin commit + PIN bump in build_air_bridge.py: yours to commit; I prepare/apply working tree on your go), est. device per fixed_frag miss ~1.1 s -> ~0.15 s, c6l total ~60 s -> ~10 s; (2) then a background prewarm worker at creation for the default variant + the formats CA actually binds (BGRA8/RGBA16F/R8 sets observed in logs), with draw waiting only if not ready - exact (same compile, wait-before-use); (3) then the 59% plan-miss rate from ui60.
